destinations.name: Paris
destinations.summary: Wrought-iron icon rising above the Seine.
destinations.story: Gustave Eiffel's company built the tower for the 1889 World's Fair in Paris. With its antennas it now stands about 330 metres tall, and it was the tallest structure in the world until 1930. Visitors can climb the stairs or ride a lift to the upper platforms for views across the city.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of the Eiffel Tower in dark silhouette against a golden evening sky.

destinations.name: Paris
destinations.summary: A former royal palace holding one of the world's great art collections.
destinations.story: The Louvre began as a medieval fortress and later became a royal palace before opening as a public museum in 1793. I. M. Pei's glass pyramid, unveiled in 1989, now marks the main entrance in the Cour Napoléon.

stamp.title: Louvre
stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of the glass pyramid of the Louvre between two palace wings at dusk.

destinations.name: London
destinations.summary: A Victorian bascule and suspension bridge over the Thames.
destinations.story: Tower Bridge opened in 1894. It combines bascule spans, which lift to let tall ships through, with suspension sections at either end. High walkways between its two towers now include a glass-floored viewing gallery above the river.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of the twin towers and walkway of Tower Bridge over the Thames under a blue sky.

destinations.name: Rome
destinations.summary: The great Roman amphitheatre at the heart of the ancient city.
destinations.story: Construction of the Colosseum began under Emperor Vespasian around 70 to 72 CE, and it opened in 80 CE. The amphitheatre held tens of thousands of spectators for gladiator contests and public shows. Earthquakes and stone-robbing left it partly ruined, but its arcaded outline is still one of the most recognisable in the world.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of the arched tiers of the Colosseum in warm evening light.

destinations.name: Istanbul
destinations.summary: A small tower on a rocky islet at the mouth of the Bosphorus.
destinations.story: Known in Turkish as Kız Kulesi, the tower stands on a small islet just off the Üsküdar shore. It has existed in various forms for centuries and has served as a lighthouse and a lookout. Boats run out to it from the shore, and from the water the skyline of mosques and minarets on the European side is spread out behind it.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of the Maiden's Tower on its islet with mosque domes and minarets across the Bosphorus at sunset.

destinations.name: Barcelona
destinations.summary: Gaudí's unfinished basilica of spires and sculpted light.
destinations.story: Construction of the basilica began in 1882, and Antoni Gaudí took over the design the following year, devoting the rest of his life to it. Building has continued for well over a century and is funded largely by visitors and donations. Its towers and facades blend Gothic structure with forms drawn from nature.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of the tall slender spires of the Sagrada Família against a golden sky.

destinations.name: Santorini
destinations.summary: Whitewashed cliffside houses above a flooded volcanic caldera.
destinations.story: Santorini's crescent shape is what remains of a volcano that erupted in the Bronze Age, leaving a sea-filled caldera. The village of Oia stretches along the northern cliff, known for its whitewashed houses, blue-domed churches and evening views across the water.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of white cubic houses and blue domes cascading down a cliff above the sea on Santorini.

destinations.name: Venice
destinations.summary: A city built on water, where the main street is a canal.
destinations.story: Venice spreads across more than a hundred small islands in a lagoon in northern Italy, linked by bridges and canals. The Grand Canal winds through the middle in a great S-shape, lined with palaces and crossed by the Rialto Bridge. Boats of every kind, from vaporetti to gondolas, are the everyday way to get around.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of Venetian palaces, a tall bell tower and a gondola on the Grand Canal at sunset.

destinations.name: Amsterdam
destinations.summary: Seventeenth-century canals lined with narrow gabled houses.
destinations.story: Amsterdam's concentric canal ring was dug during the Dutch Golden Age in the 17th century and is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Tall, narrow merchant houses with gabled facades line the water, many topped with hoisting beams once used to lift goods to the upper floors.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of narrow gabled Dutch canal houses reflected in still water.

destinations.name: Prague
destinations.summary: A medieval stone bridge lined with Baroque statues.
destinations.story: Charles Bridge crosses the Vltava River and once linked Prague's Old Town with the castle district. Its foundation stone was laid in 1357 under Charles IV, and the bridge was completed in the early 15th century. The pedestrian walkway is flanked by statues, most of them added in the Baroque period.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of the arched stone Charles Bridge with its statues and a Gothic tower at golden hour.

destinations.name: Athens
destinations.summary: The rocky citadel crowned by the Parthenon.
destinations.story: The Acropolis rises above Athens as a fortified rock with temples that date mostly from the 5th century BCE, the era of Pericles. The Parthenon, dedicated to the goddess Athena, is its best-known building, and conservation work continues on the site today.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of the columns and pediment of the Parthenon on a rocky hill under a warm sky.

destinations.name: Lisbon
destinations.summary: A fortified tower on the Tagus, built in the Age of Discoveries.
destinations.story: Belém Tower was built in the early 16th century to guard the mouth of the Tagus River and to greet returning ships. Its Manueline architecture mixes maritime motifs with the cross of the Order of Christ, and it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site together with the nearby Jerónimos Monastery.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of Belém Tower with its turrets and battlements rising from the river at sunset.

destinations.name: Edinburgh
destinations.summary: A fortress on an extinct volcano above Scotland's capital.
destinations.story: Edinburgh Castle stands on Castle Rock, the remains of an extinct volcano, overlooking the Old Town and New Town. Its buildings span many centuries, and it houses the Honours of Scotland, the Scottish crown jewels. A gun is fired from the battery at one o'clock every day except Sundays.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of Edinburgh Castle on its dark crag beneath a pale moon.

destinations.name: Reykjavík
destinations.summary: A concrete church whose stepped tower recalls basalt columns.
destinations.story: Hallgrímskirkja is one of Reykjavík's tallest structures. Guðjón Samúelsson's design is often said to evoke the basalt lava columns found in Iceland, and construction took decades, from 1945 to 1986. The tower has an observation deck with views across the colourful rooftops.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of Hallgrímskirkja's stepped tower under green and violet northern lights.

destinations.name: Geirangerfjord
destinations.summary: A narrow fjord framed by steep cliffs and waterfalls.
destinations.story: Geirangerfjord is a branch of Storfjorden in western Norway and, with Nærøyfjord, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Sheer mountainsides drop into deep water, and waterfalls such as the Seven Sisters tumble down the cliffs.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of a still fjord between steep snow-capped cliffs with waterfalls and a small ferry.

destinations.name: Zermatt
destinations.summary: The pyramid-shaped peak above a car-free Alpine village.
destinations.story: The Matterhorn rises 4,478 metres on the border between Switzerland and Italy. Edward Whymper's party made the first ascent in 1865 from Zermatt, a triumph that ended in tragedy when four of the seven climbers died on the descent. Zermatt itself is largely car-free.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of the sharp snow-capped Matterhorn above a line of pine trees.

destinations.name: Florence
destinations.summary: Brunelleschi's red-tiled dome crowning Florence's cathedral.
destinations.story: The great dome of Santa Maria del Fiore, designed by Filippo Brunelleschi, was completed in 1436 without a conventional wooden supporting frame. Visitors can climb the dome and the neighbouring Giotto's Bell Tower for views across Renaissance Florence.
altNames: Cattedrale di Santa Maria del Fiore

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of the red-tiled dome and bell tower of Florence Cathedral in warm light.

destinations.name: Budapest
destinations.summary: A Gothic Revival landmark on the banks of the Danube.
destinations.story: The Hungarian Parliament Building was designed by Imre Steindl and opened in stages from the late 19th century. Its long symmetrical facade and central dome face the Danube, and its interior is richly decorated with gilded detail.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of the lit Hungarian Parliament Building reflected in the Danube at night.

destinations.name: Neuschwanstein
destinations.summary: A fairy-tale castle perched above an Alpine valley in Bavaria.
destinations.story: King Ludwig II of Bavaria commissioned Neuschwanstein in 1869 as a personal retreat, and it was never finished in his lifetime. Its turrets and towers, set against forested mountains near Füssen, are often said to have inspired later fairy-tale castles.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of a white castle with blue conical towers on a wooded hill.

destinations.name: Hallstatt
destinations.summary: A lakeside village below limestone cliffs in the Salzkammergut.
destinations.story: Hallstatt sits on the shore of Hallstätter See in Austria's Salzkammergut region and is part of a UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape. Salt has been mined here for thousands of years, and the site gave its name to the Hallstatt culture of the early Iron Age.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of lakeside chalets and a church spire beneath a snow-capped mountain.

destinations.name: Cinque Terre
destinations.summary: Pastel houses stacked above the Ligurian Sea.
destinations.story: Manarola is one of five villages that make up Italy's Cinque Terre on the Ligurian coast, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Terraced vineyards and footpaths link the villages, whose colourful houses cling to steep cliffs above the sea.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of pastel houses stacked on a hillside above boats on the sea.

destinations.name: Meteora
destinations.summary: Monasteries balanced on towering sandstone pillars.
destinations.story: At Meteora in central Greece, Eastern Orthodox monasteries stand on top of enormous rock pillars. Monastic building here dates from the 14th century onward, and several of the monasteries remain active today. The site is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of three tall sandstone pillars crowned with small monasteries.

destinations.name: Cappadocia
destinations.summary: Fairy chimneys, cave dwellings and morning balloons.
destinations.story: In central Turkey, volcanic ash has been eroded into cones and pillars known as fairy chimneys. People carved homes, churches and storage rooms into the soft rock, and the Göreme area is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Hot-air balloons drift over the valleys at sunrise.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of rock cones and colourful hot-air balloons rising in a pink sky.
